title: eIDAS: trusted lists and qualification
description: The eIDAS profile (SimpleSign.Europe.Eidas) against the Sandbox's list of trusted lists, through the library and the CLI: the faults of the LOTL and the TL, the qualification of each signature (QESig, QESeal, AdESig-QC, AdESig) and of its time-stamps (QTSA). Tags name the items of docs/playbooks/eidas-checklist.md. Not cross-validated with EU DSS: the TestBench does not compare DSS's qualification yet.

sections.title: Trusted lists (LOTL and TL)
sections.description: The anchors come from the Sandbox's LOTL and the list it points to, each checked against the certificate of its operator (the LOTL's, then the one the LOTL names). A list that is expired, signed by another key or changed gives no anchors: signing is refused, validation finds no chain. For validation an expired national list is kept and the eidas policy's TLNotExpired (FAIL) judges it; an expired LOTL is always refused.

steps.title: Sign with a qualified certificate the Sandbox's lists vouch for
steps.description: The LOTL is checked with its operator's certificate, the TL with the one the LOTL names; the signer chains to the CA/QC service.

steps.title: TL signed by another key: refused
steps.description: The national TL is signed by a key other than the one the LOTL names for its operator: it must not be used, so there are no anchors and the eidas policy refuses to sign (UntrustedRoot).

steps.title: TL changed after signing: refused
steps.description: The TL's content changed after it was signed, so its XML signature breaks: no anchors, signing refused.

steps.title: Expired TL: refused for signing
steps.description: The TL is past its NextUpdate: for signing an outdated list gives no anchors, so the signature is refused.

steps.title: LOTL signed by another key: refused
steps.description: The LOTL is signed by a key other than its operator's: nothing it points to can be trusted, so signing is refused.

steps.title: LOTL changed after signing: refused
steps.description: The LOTL changed after it was signed: its signature breaks, nothing is trusted, signing refused.

steps.title: Expired LOTL: refused
steps.description: The LOTL is past its NextUpdate: an expired LOTL is always refused, so there are no anchors and signing is refused.

steps.title: Validate under the eidas profile
steps.description: Validates the tl-ok file under the eidas profile and policy with good lists: TOTAL_PASSED and qualified as QESig (qualified certificate, key on a QSCD).

steps.title: Validate with a fake TL: no chain, not under eIDAS
steps.description: Validates the same file while the TL has another signer: no anchors, so NO_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN_FOUND, and the qualification is N/A because the signature is not under eIDAS at all.

steps.title: Validate with an expired TL: TLNotExpired fails
steps.description: Validates it while the TL has expired: for validation the list is kept but the policy's TLNotExpired fails, so the result is INDETERMINATE / TRY_LATER and the qualification 'Indeterminate QESig' (it would be QESig with a current list).

steps.title: Validate with a fake LOTL: no chain
steps.description: Validates it while the LOTL has another signer: nothing is trusted, NO_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN_FOUND.

sections.title: Qualification of the signature (TS 119 615, TS 119 172-4)
sections.description: The CA/QC service of the Sandbox's TL, its Qualifications extension and the QC statements of each signer give the qualification of the signature: QESig and QESeal (qualified, key on a QSCD), AdESig-QC (qualified, no QSCD), AdESig (not qualified, or under a CA/PKC service).

steps.title: Qualified certificate without a QSCD
steps.description: Signs with a qualified certificate (QcCompliance) whose key is not on a QSCD: an advanced signature supported by a qualified certificate, AdESig-QC, not QESig.

steps.title: Qualified seal certificate on a QSCD
steps.description: Signs with a qualified certificate for electronic seals (QcType eseal) on a QSCD: QESeal, the seal counterpart of QESig.

steps.title: QSCD declared by the trusted list (QCWithQSCD)
steps.description: The certificate has no QcSSCD, but its policy is QCP-n-qscd and the TL's Qualifications extension says QCWithQSCD for it.

steps.title: Certificate without QC statements
steps.description: Signs with a certificate that has no QC statements: an advanced electronic signature only (AdESig).

steps.title: QC statements under a CA/PKC service
steps.description: The certificate claims QcCompliance and QcSSCD, but its CA is listed as CA/PKC: the list does not vouch for it as qualified.

steps.title: A policy that asks for a qualified certificate on a QSCD refuses a non-qualified one
steps.description: Signs with the non-qualified certificate under a policy that sets QcCompliance and QcSSCD to FAIL: a service that must make qualified signatures refuses it (CertificateNotQualified).

steps.title: The same policy signs with a qualified certificate on a QSCD
steps.description: The same policy with the default qualified certificate on a QSCD: the signature is made and qualified as QESig.

sections.title: Time-stamps (TSA/QTST)
sections.description: A time-stamp is a qualified electronic time-stamp when a TSA/QTST service of the lists, granted at its time, issued it. The eidas signing policy refuses a TSA that is not trusted or whose certificate is revoked.

steps.title: B-T with the qualified TSA
steps.description: Signs at B-T with the Sandbox's main TSA, listed as a TSA/QTST service: the signature is QESig and its time-stamp a qualified electronic time-stamp (QTSA).

steps.title: B-T with a non-qualified TSA (a TSA service)
steps.description: Signs at B-T with a TSA listed only as a TSA service: the signature is still QESig, but its time-stamp is not qualified (TSA).

steps.title: B-T with the withdrawn TSA, whose certificate is revoked: refused
steps.description: Signs at B-T with the withdrawn TSA, whose certificate is revoked: the eidas signing policy refuses its token (TimestampCertificateRevoked).

steps.title: B-T with a TSA outside the lists: refused
steps.description: Signs at B-T with a TSA that is in none of the lists: its token is not trusted, refused (TimestampUntrusted).

steps.title: CA/QC withdrawn after the signature: still qualified by its history
steps.description: The time-stamp proves the signature existed while the root's CA/QC service was granted (its ServiceHistory).
